records.name: Effective Altruism at Penn
records.summary: A Penn student group that uses evidence to work out how to do the most good. It runs an intro fellowship for new members, holds talks and discussions, and shares resources on giving and careers.
records.what_you_do: Join the Slack or the mailing list to hear about events and opportunities. Students who want to help run things can email the club about organizing or taking on a leadership role.

schedule.text: No fixed meeting time is listed. Events and fellowship news are announced through the Slack and mailing list.

first_step.how: Join the Slack and the mailing list. The introductory fellowship has its own application, so check the fellowship page when a round opens.
first_step.basis: Anyone can join the Slack and mailing list; only the fellowship asks for an application.

records.notes: Directory status field reads INACTIVE, but its active flag is true and the directory gives a fellowship deadline of February 18, 2026. The fellowship page announces a Fall 2026 fellowship without a date. Active status rests on those 2026 items.

records.name: Global Research and Consulting (GRC)
records.summary: A student-run consulting group at Wharton. Members work on real problems for global clients in many industries and build a close group of students who want hands-on experience.
records.what_you_do: Members take on consulting cases for clients, go to information sessions and coffee chats, and take part in case competitions, including one listed for fall 2026.

schedule.text: Recruits each semester. Information sessions and coffee chats come before each application round.

first_step.how: Go to an information session or coffee chat, then apply and interview in the next recruiting round. Sign up for the listserv to hear when it opens.
first_step.basis: Joining takes an application and an interview, though no prior consulting experience is needed.

records.notes: Directory status reads INACTIVE, but its active flag is true. The directory lists a Bain case competition for F'26 (fall 2026), and the club site lists 2026 case competition items with no month, so no last_sign_of_life month is recorded. The directory marks the club as not accepting members right now, so the next recruiting round is the way in. The club site also lists 2026 high school and pre-collegiate items; these were not used because the club link to them is unclear.

records.name: Grey Matters at Penn
records.summary: A student group that publishes neuroscience writing for students of every major. Members write articles and research pieces, and the group makes free podcasts with Penn faculty.
records.what_you_do: Writers, editors, artists, podcast makers, and social media helpers can each get involved. Articles and episodes appear on the group's website.

schedule.text: No meeting schedule is listed. Work runs through the writing, editing, art and podcast teams.

first_step.how: Fill in the interest form linked on the group's website, then choose a team.
first_step.basis: Joining starts with an interest form, and the directory marks an application as required, so the next step is not fully clear.

records.notes: Directory status reads INACTIVE, but the club's own site lists articles dated August 11, 2026 and January 18, 2026, and an Instagram post shown on the site dated April 24, 2026. The directory contact is a single first name at a Penn address that looks personal, so it was left out. The directory gives a founding date of January 15, 2025.

records.name: Heart Health @ Penn
records.summary: A Penn student group that raises awareness of heart disease and serves West Philadelphia. Members learn CPR, share health information, and can volunteer at Penn hospitals and shadow physicians.
records.what_you_do: Apply in the fall round. The club has four committees: CPR and advocacy, Philly public health, physician engagement, and women's cardiac health. Pre-med members can volunteer at hospitals and shadow doctors.

schedule.text: Fall 2026 application deadline was Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 11:59 pm.

first_step.how: The fall 2026 application deadline passed on September 19, 2026. Email the club to ask about the next round or any openings.
first_step.basis: Joining needs a written application before a student knows what the group is like.

records.notes: Directory status reads INACTIVE, but its active flag is true. The club's own application form is titled Fall 2026 and states a 2026 deadline. No club website is listed in the directory.

records.name: FIMRC at Penn
records.summary: The Penn chapter of an international medical relief group that supports healthcare for families in low resource areas. Members work on committees, help raise funds, and join a yearly project and, when offered, international volunteer trips.
records.what_you_do: Apply to a committee (global health, international advocacy, community outreach, or marketing), attend meetings, help fundraise, and take part in the yearly Adopt-a-Project and international volunteer trips.

schedule.text: Meets year round, with an annual Adopt-a-Project.

first_step.how: Apply through the committee application form. The fall 2026 round had a September 25 deadline, so email the club to ask about the next round.
first_step.basis: Joining needs a committee application before a student knows what the group is like.

records.notes: Directory status reads INACTIVE, but its active flag is true. The club website shows no dated items (footer year 2022 only). The 2026 evidence is the committee application form, titled Fall 2026. Its September 25 deadline and October 7 first meeting are written without a year, so no last_sign_of_life month is recorded.

records.name: Government and Politics Association
records.summary: Penn's largest student political group, built around all-party discussion. It runs a discussion group, debate and speaker events, a student political review, and a policy advocacy forum with a yearly trip to Washington.
records.what_you_do: Anyone can attend events. Students can join the Polybian Society discussion group with no requirements, or apply to a committee, the Penn Political Review, or the Forum for Legislative Action, which have short application processes.

schedule.text: No fixed meeting time is listed. Events and discussion sessions are announced through the listserv and the website.

first_step.how: Attend a public event or join the listserv from the website. Polybian has no membership requirements. Committees, the Penn Political Review, and the Forum have brief applications.
first_step.basis: Anyone can attend events and Polybian has no membership requirements, but some groups ask for an application.

records.notes: Owner judgment call: this is a student political group that describes itself as all-partisan (discussion, debate, publication, policy advocacy). It is not a party club, campaign or PAC, so it is published as nonpartisan. Directory status reads INACTIVE, but its active flag is true. The site notice says Apply by 09/18 with no year. The Fall '26 Member Application form, now closed to new responses, supplies the year, so no last_sign_of_life month is recorded. The directory lists two different committee form links; the one used here is the member application. The other form (Section Board Applications) has no year and was not used. The directory says anyone can attend events; open_to is set to students until the owner confirms.

notes: Batch of 20 Penn clubs, all listed INACTIVE in the directory, though nearly all carry an active flag of true. Six full records were written (Effective Altruism, GRC, Grey Matters, Heart Health, FIMRC, Government and Politics Association), each backed by a 2026 item from the club's own site or form, or in one case a 2026 deadline in the directory. The other 14 are held back with status unknown and no summary, because no dated activity inside the last 12 months was found or the site had no usable content. Instagram, Facebook and GroupMe were not used as sources. Personal-looking student addresses on the directory were left out. Owner judgment call: the Government and Politics Association is a student political group that calls itself all-partisan; it is published as nonpartisan and open_to is set to students pending owner confirmation.
